title: Quantinuum and HQS Simulate 21-Spin NMR Spectrum on 42 Qubits With 1,400+ Two-Qubit Gate Circuits
key_facts: Quantinuum and German software firm HQS Quantum Simulations ran a digital simulation of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy on Quantinuum's H2-1 trapped-ion quantum computer.
The target was the proton NMR spectrum of 1,2-di-tert-butyl-diphosphane, a 22-spin molecule (two phosphorus and twenty hydrogen nuclei).
A projection cut the problem from 22 physical spins to a 21-spin effective model and reduced two-qubit gates per step from 69 to 20.
The run reproduced a double-peak structure at 3.9-4.3 ppm that earlier 22-qubit hardware experiments struggled to resolve, with resolution of about 0.07 ppm.
The authors note classical solvers such as Spinach are still more efficient for routine liquid-state NMR today.
Results are in an arXiv pre-print.
quote_evidence: The benchmark modeled the liquid-state proton NMR spectrum of 1,2-di-tert-butyl-diphosphane, a classically challenging 22-spin heteronuclear molecule.
By maintaining high gate fidelity... the H2-1 hardware run successfully reproduced the double-peak structure with a spectral resolution of approximately 0.07 ppm.
While the authors note that classical solvers like Spinach remain more computationally efficient for routine high-field liquid-state spectroscopy today...
why_it_matters_hint: A chemistry-style benchmark on real quantum hardware, but ordinary computers still do this task better.
notes: The article body never mentions '42 qubits' or '1,400+ circuits' from the headline, so those figures are not used. Pre-print, no outside review.
